The problem is that ethrex was restarted during 6248 right after lodestar-nethermind-1 6247 block. Then ethrex actually manages to propose a block in 6248 but based on 6246 and the same ethrex gets to propose twice in a row (plus lighthouse-ethrex-1 which is probably on the same situation), creating a chain of blocks that should be reorged (and they were). Now, there may be still a bug in Erigon as it should have never been sent an FCU to 6250 cause that chain should never have been canonical on any non-ethrex node Ethrex continues producing orphaned blocks until it eventually catches up in 6264 <@412614104222531604> the reorg thing you reported was from prysm-erigon-1 or some other erigon? I'm interested in chasing this down cause this should definitely not happen nimbus-erigon-1 hmm, the first erigon node to propose after the ethrex fork is prysm, will see if I find similar reports there. <@&1417820113981145228> another quick question, do you guys queue payload if it's slightly earlier than current slot? ok, i see the issue with nimbus<>erigon, ill fix it tomorrow (can resync for now, ive backed up the logs) we do do you mind checking for slot 7218 payload that you queued it? 🙏 we received the block 802ms into the slot, the block was processed at 823ms, the envelope was received at 812ms, so yes, we queued it, it was received ~10ms before the block was imported ah we queue in that situation I think the problem is when the payload is received before the block itself, but we also queue that the issue is that we do not understand why we don't get Nimbus' payloads at all, one explanation would be if we drop them before the slot starts, but that's not it dont know if it is related, but buildoor and the prysm node it is attached to is unable to see proposer preferences from nimbus too. oh interesting, is it only Nimbus? yeah seems like it i m trying to reproduce it locally well i dont see teku either but teku is not looking good anyways cc <@654267572107083777> you guys probably don't like us is the peering not good between nimbus/prysm? The client graph shows us connected but we don't get your payloads from time to time we have had this since Svalbard don't know if it's on our side or yours, I think it's ours cause other clients seem to get them so even if you dislike us, those clients should forward payloads to us unless of course no one is forwarding payloads 😛 is there evidence the payloads are just invalid, or? they seem to show up mostly ok in Dora though some apparently go missing, which seems specific to Nimbus they are fine, we just don't get them, so we build on empty and we are reorged out 7818 for example we only request by root after we have produced the block 7819 on empty and other attesters don't like us and vote for 7818 full and only then we realize that the payload exists somewhere and request it hm, wonder if they're being distributed in general, through gossip because if they are, then specific nimbus/prysm peering issues shouldn't matter just get them through any of the other CLs by gossip I mean, not waiting for request by root yeah that's what I meant above if peers aren't forwarding payloads 🙂 We should be getting them, but for some reason we don't well, in theory this should be a measurable thing.
